summary: Receives Windows multi-touch events as either raw event FIFO rows or an ID table, with optional panel-relative coordinates, occlusion handling, mouse support, and callbacks.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Enable multi-touch input

key_params.name: outputtype
key_params.note: Choose raw event FIFO or current ID table output

key_params.name: panel
key_params.note: Panel used for relative touch coordinates and occlusion testing

key_params.name: relativeid
key_params.note: Report touch IDs relative to the selected panel

key_params.name: relativepos
key_params.note: Report touch positions relative to the selected panel

key_params.name: occlusion
key_params.note: Restrict touch events by panel hierarchy

key_params.name: occbydepth
key_params.note: Filter touch events by panel depth layer

key_params.name: occdepthlayer

key_params.name: mouse
key_params.note: Include mouse input as touch-style rows

key_params.name: callbacks

key_params.name: executeloc

common_gotchas: The operator uses the Windows standard multi-touch API and is not a portable macOS touch input solution.
Mouse emulation can share ID 1 with the first touch, so mixed mouse/touch logic needs guards.
Raw Events and ID Table outputs have different table shapes and should not be swapped without downstream changes.
Panel occlusion depends on hierarchy and depth-layer settings, so touch routing should be validated visually.
key_concepts: Captures multitouch panel events into a DAT table.
Output can be raw FIFO events or one-row-per-finger ID table state.
Panel, relative id, relative position, and occlusion parameters scope the captured touch region.
Threshold, mouse, callback, and retention controls shape event volume and semantics.
